incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: Capacity alarm fired for prod-us-west-1 - autoscaler lagging, queue depth > 1200 for inference-queue-high. Triggered 2x escalation.

pagerduty-bot: Pager  -> ashley (oncall) - page fired at 2026-03-17T18:24:16Z.

ashley (oncall): acked. I'm looking. Any customer-facing degradations?

samir (infra): metrics show sustained provision latency - node pool API calls returning 504s from cloud provider for last 5m. Autoscaler has 0 successful adds in that window.

jason (serving): queue backlog at dispatcher: "inflight_tokens" spiking, per-route latency 95p -> 18s. Affected routes: realtime-chat, autocomplete-high. Non-critical batch routes fine.

kai (sre): adding context: kvcache warmup pressure low, prefix miss rate up 70% -> increases token generation time. Could be both autoscale and cold cache contributing.

ashley (oncall): plan: 1) manual spin up a small hotpool as stopgap, 2) fail-fast non-critical routes to lower-tier model, 3) escalate to cloud provider if quota errors. Who can run manual spin?

jason (serving): I'll run manual spin for hotpool-1 - starting smaller VM family to bypass spot delays. Running command:
```
./opsctl pool create --name hotpool-1 --region us-west-1 --nodes 6 --type g5 --tags hotpool,ephemeral
```

samir (infra): seeing API errors: "QuotaExceeded: Cannot allocate more IPs" on VPC side. That explains provisioning hang. Raising support ticket with provider now, but we need an immediate workaround.

ashley (oncall): ok, fallback: jason, can we temporarily re-route realtime-chat to dedicated warm instances in prod-us-west-2 (cross-region)? Traffic will be slightly higher latency but keeps customers alive.

jason (serving): yes, creating a route override: /routes/realtime-chat -> model: rwd-realtime-v1@us-west-2; applying canary now (20%).

pagerduty-bot: Pager acknowledged by ashley (oncall). Escalation to level-2 after 10m if not resolved.

kai (sre): I'm throttling ingest on low-priority tenants via circuit-breaker to reduce queue pressure. Pushing config: `circuit.breaker.low_priority=true`

samir (infra): cloud provider ticket created INC-987654 - quota team looking. Workaround: using existing reserved IP pool from backup-VPC. I'll attach reserved-ips to new nodes to bypass soft quota. Doing that now.

jason (serving): hotpool spin succeeded with reserved IPs. Nodes joined runtime, KV cache warmup started. Dispatcher draining backlog to new nodes.

ashley (oncall): good. What's the customer impact summary so far?

kai (sre): customer visible: increased 500s ~ 2.1% of requests for realtime-chat during peak 18:10-18:30. Latency spikes for autocomplete-high; we routed that to a fallback model in us-west-2 with 700ms extra p95. No data plane errors/exposure.

samir (infra): provider confirmed soft quota gating provisioning. They've bumped soft quota temporarily; ticket still open. We'll schedule permanent quota increase with provider tomorrow.

jason (serving): backlog reduced from 1200 -> 120 in 12 minutes after hotpool attach and circuit breakers. Autoscaler metrics now showing successful adds; scaling decisions resuming.

ashley (oncall): pager status: acknowledged, mitigation in place, impact reduced. I'll handoff to oncall rotation at 19:00. Leaving runbook steps in incident doc. If dashboards show queue depth > 500 after 19:00, escalate to L2.

pagerduty-bot: Pager closed for initial page (ack). Will reopen if escalation criteria met.

incident-bot: Incident note appended: "hotpool warmup / provider IP quota caused autoscaler provisioning failures -> manual hotpool attach + cross-region routing + circuit-breaker mitigations restored service".

ashley (oncall): TL;DR: root cause likely provider soft quota on IPs -> autoscaler couldn't provision -> queue backlog. Mitigations: reserved IP attach, manual hotpool, route fallback, throttle low-priority traffic. Follow-ups: permanent quota increase, improve autoscaler fallback to use reserved pools, add alert for VPC quota errors.

kai (sre): I'll file follow-up RFC and postmortem. Moving to monitoring state. Thanks team :thumbsup:

ashley (oncall): handing off to night oncall @jordan at 19:00. Please DM if anything flares.
